contexts.text: May serve for... the impregnation of the ovule.
Seeds... are impregnated with the most subtle substances...
That men... impregnate their blood with like things...
In the seed there is the soul; for from it the impregnation is effected.
Like birds impregnated with eggs, and without nests...
In the same proportion, the good he does is impregnated with that evil.
No seed could (then) be impregnated from its inmosts.
From this sphere the inmost of every seed is impregnated.
This is... how (the seed) produces impregnation.
That it is allowable to love an impregnated wife.
In certain places in the bosom of the earth there are minerals impregnated with gold, silver, copper, and iron.
